annotationRationale: The main route uses angle identities and factoring, then counts distinct cosine values in the open interval. The alternative reveals the persistent root directly through sum-to-product and avoids solving a quadratic in cosine.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Algebra is reasonable for the reduction to a factored parameter equation; no obvious subject repair is warranted.

review.questionCheck: Dividing by the positive sin x gives (2 cos x+1)(2 cos x-1-a)=0. Cosine is one-to-one on (0,π), so a second distinct solution exists exactly for -3<a<1 with a≠-2. Thus p+q+r=-4, choice A. The choices and key agree.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: There are no shared-bank methods. The LIVE route and AoPS Solutions 1 and 2 are represented by factor-in-cosine; the quadratic-formula computation is equivalent and need not be separate. AoPS Solution 3 is retained as shared-sine-factor. No further distinct accessible route is needed.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed angle identities, cosine range and quadratic factoring fit the main route; angle addition and linear inequalities support it. The cosine node's supplied scope does not itself establish injectivity, which the main explanation justifies geometrically.
review.areaCheck: Algebra is reasonable for the reduction to a factored parameter equation; no obvious subject repair is warranted.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The derived triple-angle identity and factorization are correct. The fixed root is x=2π/3. The other cosine value lies in (-1,1) exactly for -3<a<1 and coincides with -1/2 only at a=-2. Open endpoints and distinctness are handled correctly.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The cited LIVE explanation and AoPS Solutions 1 and 2 support the claimed route. The zero-product formulation safely retains the persistent root and avoids the source quadratic-formula absolute-value issue. The expanded derivation is original explanatory prose, appropriately labeled source-informed-original.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The initial division is motivated and justified. The difficult identity is derived, and the unit-semicircle explanation supplies the necessary one-to-one correspondence between cosine values and solutions.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Angle addition, double-angle identities, cosine range, quadratic factoring and simultaneous linear inequalities all occur. The injectivity conclusion is explained separately rather than attributed to parity or periodicity.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The supplied native links match the identity, range, factoring and inequality components. The cosine definition lists limited properties, so its exact CN link should not be read as an explicit monotonicity standard.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: F-TF.C.9 supports formula use, without full coverage of its proof requirements. A-SSE.B.3a and A-REI.B.4/4b support the quadratic factoring component. The cosine graph links do not establish full coverage of graphing or injectivity standards.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All listed nodes are used within their relevant scopes; the additional solution-counting consequence is justified in the explanation.

methodReviews.mathCheck: With t=x/2, the factored equation is correct. On 0<3t<3π/2, the shared sine vanishes only at 3t=π. The other branch gives y²=(a+3)/4 with 0<y<1, hence one admissible solution exactly for -3<a<1. It duplicates the persistent solution only at a=-2.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: This independently complete route accurately credits AoPS Solution 3. It derives the sum-to-product and triple-angle expressions and handles the shared factor before division. The source-informed-original designation is appropriate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The substitution and persistent-root strategy are motivated. Positivity justifies division by y and selects the unique square root; the standard one-to-one cosine branch on (0,π/2) completes the solution count.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Sine addition and subtraction, double-angle formulas, the Pythagorean identity, cosine range and linear inequalities are all used. No unexplained sum-to-product prerequisite is imported.

nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The six immediate nodes accurately describe the derivation; the triple-angle and sum-to-product consequences are derived from them.
